items.title: Agoda Doubles Premium Hotel Supply as Five-Star Search Rises
items.summary: Agoda has doubled its luxury supply and five-star searches are rising. Until it shows bookings, there’s no hard proof the platform can sell luxury.

items.title: Vrbo Exempts Some Properties From Losing Subscription Plans: Scoop
items.summary: With some hosts and property managers upset about being unable to renew or convert to subscriptions, Vrbo should be more transparent about why some listings qualify for an exemption while others don't.

items.title: Louvre Closed, Travel Warnings Mount: What France’s Protests Mean for Tourists
items.summary: Governments are updating their travel guidance as protests spread across Europe. The question for travel is whether unrest will continue beyond region's shoulder season.

items.title: Kempinski Faces Leadership Upheaval as CEO and Senior Executives Depart: Scoop
items.summary: Kempinski’s leadership upheaval raises questions about who will carry out its luxury turnaround and how it will be funded.

items.title: Third of Saudi Flights Canceled As High Profile Events Postponed
items.summary: Saudi carriers have restored service, but they can’t restore the confidence that international airlines and event organizers need. The longer foreign carriers stay out, the more Riyadh’s events-led Q4 turns into a lost quarter for hotels and for business, sporting and leisure eve

items.title: Hotels Could Become One of Ixigo’s Two Biggest Businesses
items.summary: Ixigo has the product and a steady stream of customers. What remains is the hard part of convincing budget travelers that the room they book online is the room they’ll get.

items.title: The Quiet Rise of Loveholidays on a 20-Year-Old Business Idea
items.summary: UK’s Loveholidays didn’t invent dynamic packaging — it built its muscle through scale. The big test ahead is whether it can replicate it in Europe.

items.title: Airbnb Joins Vrbo and Marriott In Paying Guests When It Rains Too Much
items.summary: The idea is that paying travelers when rain passes a certain threshold can help increase conversions among those worried about weather spoiling their plans. The question is whether guarantees will spread to other types of weather — like the extreme heat seen in Europe this summer
